ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the region where $y>0$, there is a uniform electric field along the positive $y$-axis, and in the region where $y<0$, there is a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the coordinate plane and pointing inward. An electron with mass $m$ and charge $e$ starts moving from point $A$ on the $y$-axis with an initial velocity $v_{0}$ along the positive $x$-axis. When the electron crosses the $x$-axis for the first time, it reaches point $C$; when it crosses the $x$-axis for the second time, it reaches the origin; and when it crosses the $x$-axis for the third time, it reaches point $D$. Points $C$ and $D$ are not marked in the figure. It is known that the distances from points $A$ and $C$ to the origin are $d$ and $2d$, respectively, and the gravitational force on the electron is negligible.

1. What is the magnitude of the electric field strength $E$?
2. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B$?
3. What is the time \( t \) it takes for an electron to move from \( A \) to \( D \)?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, the x-axis is horizontal to the right, the y-axis is vertical upward, and the origin O is at the intersection of the two axes. Point A is located on the positive semi-axis of the y-axis, and at A the initial velocity v_0 of the electron is along the positive x direction. Above the x-axis, multiple upward arrows are drawn and labeled E, indicating that in the y>0 region the electric field is along the positive y direction; below the x-axis, crosses are drawn and labeled B, indicating that in the y<0 region the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. The problem states that C and D are not marked in the figure. Reasoning: According to the problem, take A=(0,d). The electron is negatively charged, and the electric field E is upward, so in y>0 the electron is subjected to an electric field force downward, with acceleration magnitude eE/m and direction -y. Initially from A to the first crossing of the x-axis at C, because the initial velocity is horizontally to the right, and |OC|=2d, take C=(2d,0). In the upper half-plane the equations of motion are x=v_0 t, y=d-(eE/(2m))t^2. When reaching C, x=2d, therefore t_AC=2d/v_0; also y=0, so d=(eE/(2m))(2d/v_0)^2, solving gives E=mv_0^2/(2ed). At C, v_x=v_0, v_y=-(eE/m)t_AC=-v_0, therefore v_C=(v_0,-v_0), and the speed is sqrt(2)v_0. After entering y<0, the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. The electron is negative, and the direction of the Lorentz force makes the center of the trajectory circle be to the lower left of the velocity direction at point C; at the same time, the second crossing of the x-axis is the origin O. The circle center satisfying the geometric relation is (d,-d), and the radius R=sqrt(2)d. Circular motion in the magnetic field satisfies e v_C B = m v_C^2/R, namely B=m v_C/(eR)=m(sqrt(2)v_0)/(e sqrt(2)d)=mv_0/(ed). The circular arc from C to O is 270°, namely 3π/2 radians, so t_CO=(3π/2)R/v_C=3πd/(2v_0). When reaching O, the velocity direction is (v_0,v_0). After entering y>0 again, the initial velocity in the vertical direction is v_0, the acceleration is downward and has magnitude eE/m=v_0^2/(2d), and the time required to return to the x-axis is t_OD=2v_0/(eE/m)=4d/v_0. The total time t=t_AC+t_CO+t_OD=2d/v_0+3πd/(2v_0)+4d/v_0=3d(4+π)/(2v_0).
